notes: This contract covers the bounded timestamped regional Update Attribute Values path in the embedded development profile. A committed update-region association feeds a timestamped attribute passel; only active overlapping regional attribute triples are eligible, while passive triples remain retained without arranging reflection; the timestamped cases do not independently test that mode selector. Time-constrained recipients receive the reflection before the matching Time Advance Grant while non-time-constrained recipients receive the accepted timestamped callback immediately. Focused ordinary TAR/NMR and explicit-source Time Constrained disable/re-enable companions now drive the same overlap-qualified passel to their grant frontiers, preserving callback-before-grant ordering and the source RegionHandle metadata. A focused untimed save/restore companion now saves one queued explicit-source passel and its live retraction ledger, terminalizes the designator after saving, restores the object/update association and source RegionHandle set, delivers through Flush Queue Request, and proves post-delivery Request Retraction; RL-137 records the Requirements Lab's missing cross-service regional attribute save/restore relation. A matching default-source save/restore companion preserves one ordinary-registration passel, its private default source, supplied-empty callback projection, and live retraction ledger through an untimed snapshot before Flush Queue reflection and Request Retraction; RL-140 records the corresponding relation gap. Its timed companion retains a timestamp-eight default-source passel across a timestamp-six save boundary before restore and FQR delivery; RL-141 records the missing save-boundary relation. A class-level regional Request Attribute Value Update companion now supplies a timestamped provider response through the official Provide callback and proves the same TSO ordering and source-region preservation. Separate default-source companions drive ordinary/default-region passels to FQR, TARA, and NMRA and through a Time Constrained disable/re-enable transition; they verify the supplied-empty callback RegionHandleSet remains stable and that the queued reflection is delivered exactly once before the post-re-enable grant. The federation-owned recipient ledger lets Retract suppress the pending constrained delivery and invoke Request Retraction for the delivered nonconstrained recipient; the recipient's Convey Region Designator Sets switch gates optional sent-region callback metadata. A direct disjoint-region regression proves that a qualifying regional update—time-regulating with a TSO-preferred submitted attribute—returns a valid designator even though no subscription overlaps; the ledger supports legal Retract and later terminal classification without retaining typed passels. Separate immediate- and time-constrained-recipient callback-boundary regressions accept initial strict overlap, commit the recipient region to the valid disjoint interval [2, 3] before dispatch, and suppress Reflect Attribute Values from the current projection. The immediate case terminally closes its recipient ledger state and proves that a still-legal Retract emits no Request Retraction; the time-constrained case reaches only its time-6 grant, after which the producer's strict boundary makes the designator no longer retractable without manufacturing a callback. A focused source-association replacement regression additionally proves that a queued passel captured under sourceRegionA is suppressed after unassociation and association of sourceRegionB, while a later passel uses sourceRegionB; it does not claim replacement semantics for every transport or lifecycle mode. Complete default-region/re-enable coverage beyond these bounded role-transition companions, timed/durable restore, remote transport, package evidence, and conformance remain outside this slice.
